title: Prove the fixed five-call border needs two repair cuts (no κ)
body:
## Summary

The fixed five-call reflection border in PR6398 needs exactly **two distinct repair cuts** when repairs are linear, central-only and independent of the three stage variables. This is a **scoped algebraic proof with exact finite evidence**, not a new kappa or supplier admission.

At any one of the six cuts, invertibility forces one repair matrix:

```text
required repair = inverse(suffix) * target * inverse(prefix)
B = 1 and B = -1 force different repairs at every cut
```

This rules out arbitrary rank and arbitrarily long central-only blocks at one location. A diagonal similarity covers every nonzero border parameter over every field of characteristic other than two. Ali Romman's existing two rank-one corrections attain the lower bound; the new contribution is the six-cut obstruction and unique-correction table. The predecessor's native identity, prices and search results are cited premises, not audit deliverables.

## Evidence

Before this result, PR6398 exhibited two direct corrections and left different recovery methods open. The new proof excludes every repair confined to one cut, even if its rank or scalar complexity increases.

Both full direct modes print `PASS_BORDER_SINGLE_CORRECTION`. Each enumerates 36 cut/parameter witnesses with explicit frozen-repair failures, 36 normalized coefficient-table checks, 48 attaining fixtures and five domain/singularity rejection controls. The normal and optimized registered commands took 0.154 and 0.163 seconds locally, respectively, rounded up. Generated receipts bind all six package files by SHA256. Package replay prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`; publication preflight prints `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`, including the base's source-history binding.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/border-single-correction/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/border-single-correction/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/border-single-correction
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/border-single-correction --check-source-history
```

Other hosts may substitute CPython 3.12. The verifier uses only the standard library and writes its generated receipt to stdout. The written proof supplies the all-parameter quantifiers; the fixed rational checks are exact corroboration and a bounded-degree coefficient certificate.

## Limitations

Four arbitrary input fields, fixed original factors, fixed cut selection and a formal identity modulo `S^2=1` are explicit hypotheses. Retuning the word, additional workspace, adaptive cut selection, stage-dependent operations and approximate recovery remain outside the theorem. A concrete central operator with no negative character is outside the obstruction.

No complete tariff optimum, recursive precision transfer, physical realization or selected-frontier update is claimed. Lean, Docker, native/selected cold replay and predecessor root searches were not run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. The exact predecessor head is `dee2663ba0918be86993fd9d63c8d64b020f4c83`; main was refreshed at `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priority revision 8.

Produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Ali Romman for the border, open recovery question and attaining word; Cinna Davis for caller interfaces, Jacob Alan Sussman for productive recursion, and the retained native/helper/compiler/BIT/analytic lineage identified in PR6398. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19360652).

## Related open work

- #6398 supplies this exact border and its two-correction upper bound; this PR adds a sharp lower bound on distinct repair locations and does not recount its price or native construction.
- #6391 studies a different three-stage overlapping-output completion invoice. It does not repair this fixed border, and this result does not establish a tariff comparison with that proposal.

## Open next questions

- Can a changed two-cut recovery beat the complete price of the existing two rank-one queries? Start with both explicit cut operations and their signed invoice; the location bound does not settle tariff optimality.
- Can a stage-sensitive operation or changed original factor produce a favorable exact caller? Price the middle-stage dependence, inverse access, restoration and cleanup before extending the construction.
